messages:
Ava: Quick follow-up to the quant-attn RFC — I sketched a different approach that treats 'dequant+attn' as a composable operator with a small opset contract. Goal: make kernels able to opt into a fused path without forcing runtime-wide format changes.

Ravi: sketch? can you paste the contract here pls

Ava: sure — core ideas: 1) introduce a lightweight op 'dequant_attn' that accepts quantized Q/K/V + per-tensor/per-head scale metadata, optional fp8 metadata, and an explicit mask/rotary hint. 2) runtime falls back to sequential dequant->attn if kernel not present. 3) kernels can advertise supported quant formats and constraints in the registry.

Sam: i'm worried about mask semantics. if op fuses dequant+attn, we need to keep exact same mask ordering and dtype promotion as our current attn impl. otherwise downstream evals will diverge.

Ava: agreed. contract includes: mask is boolean same-shape tensor (0/1), kernel must honor padding semantics and causal flag. also include an explicit "accum_dtype" field (fp16/fp32) for numerical determinism.

Ben: what about KV cache? we stream quantized KV into cache on dedicated nodes today. fusion needs to support adding quantized entries without dequantizing entire cache. is that in the plan?

Ava: good catch. plan: dequant_attn accepts either raw quantized KV slices or pre-dequantized slices. We add a separate op 'dequant_kv_append' to let kernels manage per-shard caching with quantized storage. That keeps the cache format compatible.

Marta: scaling strategy: per-head scale vs global scale? a lot of models use per-channel scale for INT4 to keep dynamic range. kernels need to report which scaling they require.

Ravi: registry change sounds heavy. how do you see the kernel advertisement API? small JSON descriptor?

Ava: yes, something like:
```
{
  "kernel_name": "fused_dequant_attn_f32_acc",
  "supported_formats": ["int8_scale_per_head","int4_scale_per_channel","fp8_e5m2"],
  "requires_mask_bool": true,
  "max_seq_len": 4096,
  "accum_dtype": "fp32"
}
```
Runtime will pick best match based on request metadata and model hints.

Ben: what about sequence lengths > max_seq_len? fallback path or split into windows?

Ava: runtime chooses fallback to non-fused path if sequence > max_seq_len for that kernel. Alternatively, kernels can declare streaming behavior and expose a window_size.

Sam: regression testing note: add deterministic eval harness that runs same prompts across fused+unfused paths and compares token-level logits within an epsilon. Should be part of the kernel onboarding checklist.

Marta: numerical stability: some fp8->fp32 accumulation patterns cause tiny bias across many tokens. We should allow a "stability_mode" flag (e.g., conservative_accum=true) and measure perf delta. Kernels can implement it if they want.

Ravi: performance question: if we allow both per-head and per-channel scales, fusion kernel complexity skyrockets. Maybe require model quantizer to choose a canonical format per model and expose that in the model manifest, so kernel selection is simpler.

Ava: yep that's in the doc: recommend canonical format in model metadata and have the runtime provide a cheap remap layer for models that deviate. remap should be optional and used only when needed.

Ben: edge case — rotary/pos emb combined with quantized Q: some kernels assume float for rotary multiply. do we pass a rotary hint (type + precomputed cos/sin in quantized form)?

Ava: include a 'rotary_hint' field: {type: "fixed", precomp_dtype: "fp16|fp32|quant8", precomp_tensor: optional}. Kernels that can't handle quantized rotary declare they need pre-dequantized precomp.

Sam: can we include a short example of op invocation for the runtime codegen?

Ava: example call in pseudocode:
```
call_op("dequant_attn", {
  q: <uint8 tensor>,
  k: <uint8 tensor>,
  v: <uint8 tensor>,
  scale_meta: {format: "int4_scale_per_channel", scales: <fp16 tensor>},
  mask: <bool tensor>,
  causal: true,
  accum_dtype: "fp32",
  rotary_hint: {type: "fixed", precomp_dtype: "fp16"}
}) -> logits
```

Marta: I like this. for kernel onboarding checklist: 1) unit tests for mask semantics, 2) kv cache appends, 3) fused/unfused parity tests, 4) perf benchmark with typical batching.

Ravi: also include a fallback policy in the runtime config: prefer_fused=true/false, allow_partial_fuse=true. we need ops-level fallbacks to avoid global perf cliffs.

Ben: owner? who takes this RFC follow-up and converts into a small PR for the registry + example kernel?

Ava: I can take the registry + contract draft. Sam and Marta can own test harness additions. Ravi please add the runtime selection flags in a follow-up.

Deploy-Bot: scheduled job: run fused-vs-unfused-e2e on staging tonight — 23:00 UTC.

Sam: thanks. I'll add the harness to the night run and include the new epsilon thresholds.

Ravi: noted — I'll start a short PR for the kernel descriptor schema and flags.

Marta: i'll stub the onboarding checklist in docs.

Ben: great, thanks all. excited to see if we can get significant perf with minimal model churn :rocket:

Ava: i'll push the draft doc and PR link here later today.
